catalog_note: sdrscan check registry. Every check names the FedRAMP rules that make it a requirement. Severity reflects the consequence of the gap for a certification decision, not the difficulty of fixing it.

checks.title: Rule-specific artifacts are referenced where they apply
checks.requirement: SDR-CSO-FRR item 7: rule-specific artifacts, if applicable.
checks.risk: A rule whose evidence lives in an unreferenced document forces the assessor to go looking, and they may not find it.
checks.remediation: Reference the artifact, or confirm none applies to this rule.

checks.title: Responses to assessor comments are recorded where comments exist
checks.requirement: SDR-CSO-FRR item 6: any responses or clarifications to the comments in the independent verification or validation.
checks.risk: An unanswered assessor comment left out of the record looks like it was never raised.
checks.remediation: Confirm no comment is outstanding, or record the response.

checks.title: Rule implementation is explained
checks.requirement: Explanation of how the rule is followed, or an explanation of the reason and resulting risk to customers for not following the rule.
checks.risk: This is the first of the seven items SDR-CSO-FRR requires for every rule; a placeholder here means the rule is undocumented.
checks.remediation: Replace the placeholder with the provider's real implementation.

checks.title: Independent validation of the rule is recorded
checks.requirement: SDR-CSO-FRR item 5: independent validation. IVV-IAS-VEF is the assessor-side rule that produces it.
checks.risk: Without independent validation nobody outside the provider has confirmed the implementation actually works.
checks.remediation: Record the independent assessor's validation statement once performed.

checks.title: Independent verification of the rule is recorded
checks.requirement: SDR-CSO-FRR item 4: independent verification. IVV-IAS-VIM is the assessor-side rule that produces it.
checks.risk: Provider self-attestation is not independent verification. Its absence is a gap an assessor will raise directly.
checks.remediation: Record the independent assessor's verification statement once performed. This has no official schema field, so it lives in the extensions companion.

checks.title: Rules not fully followed state the reason they are not followed
checks.requirement: SDR-CSO-FRR item 1 requires, for a rule that is not followed, the reason it is not followed AND the resulting risk to customers - two distinct elements. The risk is not the reason.
checks.risk: Without the reason, an assessor cannot tell WHY the rule is not followed, only what the residual risk is; the two are different facts.
checks.remediation: State the reason for not following the rule in nonimplementation_reason (or explain it in the implementation narrative) on every rule that is not Implemented.

checks.title: Rules not fully followed state the resulting customer risk
checks.requirement: SDR-CSO-FRR requires the reason AND the resulting risk to customers whenever a rule is not followed.
checks.risk: Agencies make risk-acceptance decisions from this text. Omitting it shifts an undisclosed risk onto the customer.
checks.remediation: State the risk to customers in plain terms on every rule that is not Implemented.

checks.title: Rule has a named accountable owner
checks.requirement: The status of persistent activities must always be known, which requires somebody accountable for keeping it known.
checks.risk: Unowned rules go stale between assessments because nobody is responsible for refreshing them.
checks.remediation: Assign an owning team or role, not an individual's name.

checks.title: Unimplemented rules carry senior official acceptance
checks.requirement: SDR-CSO-FRR allows verification and validation to be replaced by a senior official's acceptance of the reason for not implementing.
checks.risk: A rule marked Not Implemented with nobody accountable for that decision is an unowned risk.
checks.remediation: Name the senior official who accepted the decision and when.

checks.title: Rule text matches the canonical dataset exactly
checks.requirement: The rule text a provider answers must be the rule text FedRAMP published.
checks.risk: Paraphrasing a rule quietly changes what the provider is claiming to have met, which invalidates the answer.
checks.remediation: Never edit rule text. Regenerate from the pinned dataset.

checks.title: Rule carries a valid implementation status
checks.requirement: frrImplementationStatus must be Implemented, Not Implemented or Partially Implemented.
checks.risk: An absent or invented status leaves the reader guessing whether the rule is met.
checks.remediation: Set implementation_status on the rule in the record store.

checks.title: Provider validation of the rule is recorded
checks.requirement: Validation that the implementation is in place and working as intended, or that the reason for not implementing is accepted by a senior official.
checks.risk: Verification without validation claims the design is right but never shows it works.
checks.remediation: Record how the implementation is confirmed to be working, and how often.

checks.title: Provider verification of the rule is recorded
checks.requirement: Verification that the implementation is appropriate for the rule, or that the reason for not implementing is accepted by a senior official.
checks.risk: Without verification there is no statement that the implementation is the right one, only that something was built.
checks.remediation: Record who verified the implementation as appropriate, and how.

checks.title: Automation behind the measures is verified as accurate and sufficient
checks.requirement: SDR-CSX-KSI item 4: verification that the automation in place is accurate and sufficient to demonstrate appropriate measures, or that automation is not necessary for each measure.
checks.risk: Unverified automation is the most dangerous kind of evidence: it produces confident output nobody has checked.
checks.remediation: Record how the automation was verified, or state why automation is unnecessary for this measure.

checks.title: Indicator has evidence attached
checks.requirement: The official schema requires ksiEvidence, holding the results of the security tests used to validate the indicator.
checks.risk: A test with no recorded result is an assertion, not evidence.
checks.remediation: Attach the output of each automated method as an evidence entry.

checks.title: Evidence uses official evidence types
checks.requirement: evidenceType must be one of Log, Report, Screenshot, Configuration, Policy, Procedure or Audit Record.
checks.risk: A non-official type value makes the document fail schema validation and breaks automated ingestion.
checks.remediation: Use one of the seven official evidenceType values.

checks.title: Independent assessment of the indicator is recorded
checks.requirement: Assessors verify and validate Key Security Indicators independently of the provider, and IVV-CSX-AIA requires an annual independent assessment for 20x.
checks.risk: Self-assessed indicators carry no independent weight in a certification decision.
checks.remediation: Record the assessor's statement once the assessment is performed.

checks.title: Indicator measures and objectives are explained
checks.requirement: Explanation of measures (and their objectives) that demonstrate the Key Security Indicator, or an explanation of the reason and resulting risk to customers for not having measures available.
checks.risk: The indicator is the unit FedRAMP evaluates in 20x. An unexplained indicator contributes nothing to the certification.
checks.remediation: Describe the measures and what each is meant to demonstrate.

checks.title: Measures are validated as working as intended
checks.requirement: SDR-CSX-KSI item 5: validation that the measures are accurately produced and are in place and working as intended.
checks.risk: Verification without validation asserts the measure is the right one but never shows it runs correctly.
checks.remediation: Record how the measures are confirmed to be producing accurate output.

checks.title: Measures are verified to demonstrate the indicator
checks.requirement: SDR-CSX-KSI item 3: verification that the measures demonstrate the Key Security Indicator, or that the reason for not having them is accepted.
checks.risk: A measure that runs reliably but does not actually evidence the indicator gives false assurance.
checks.remediation: Record who confirmed that the measures evidence this indicator.

checks.title: Indicator carries a 30-day metric summary
checks.requirement: Class C providers MUST, and Class B providers SHOULD (dataset 2026.10.08.01; MUST before), include a summary of each metric over the past 30 days.
checks.risk: Without recent history an assessor sees a snapshot and cannot tell whether the control has been holding.
checks.remediation: Record the 30-day summary, ideally written by the collector rather than by hand.

checks.title: Class C indicators reference a year of daily metric data
checks.requirement: Class C providers MUST supply all daily metric data, including the status of persistent validation, up to the past year, where available.
checks.risk: Class C rests on continuous data. Summaries alone do not meet it.
checks.remediation: Reference the daily metric store, for example the collector's evidence bucket prefix.

checks.title: Indicator carries a metric summary up to the past year
checks.requirement: Class C providers MUST, and Class B providers SHOULD, include a summary of the metric up to the past year, where available.
checks.risk: A year of history is what distinguishes a sustained control from one that was fixed the week before assessment.
checks.remediation: Record the longer-run summary once that much history exists.

checks.title: Persistent measures explain their operating cycle
checks.requirement: SDR-CSX-KSI item 2: explanation of the cycle for any measures that are implemented persistently.
checks.risk: Without a stated cycle, a reader cannot tell whether a passing measure was checked this morning or last quarter.
checks.remediation: State the cycle, or confirm no measure for this indicator runs persistently.

checks.title: Indicator has a named accountable owner
checks.requirement: The status of persistent activities must always be known.
checks.risk: Unowned indicators drift, and drift in an indicator is invisible until an assessment finds it.
checks.remediation: Assign an owning team or role.

checks.title: Indicators with no published statement are marked FedRAMP pending
checks.requirement: A KSI is FedRAMP pending only when the pinned CR26 dataset gives it no statement anywhere - neither a top-level statement nor any per-class statement under varies_by_class. This is derived from the dataset, not a hardcoded list, so it cannot drift.
checks.risk: Inventing text for an indicator FedRAMP has not published would be fabrication; conversely, marking an indicator that DOES have a per-class statement as pending is a factually wrong scanner output.
checks.remediation: Leave a genuinely statement-less indicator marked FedRAMP pending until FedRAMP publishes the statement; answer any indicator that has a per-class statement.

checks.title: Indicator text matches the canonical dataset
checks.requirement: The indicator text a provider answers must be the text FedRAMP published.
checks.risk: Paraphrasing changes what is being claimed.
checks.remediation: Never edit indicator text. Regenerate from the pinned dataset.

checks.title: Indicator carries a valid implementation status
checks.requirement: ksiImplementationStatus must be one of the three official values.
checks.risk: An absent status leaves the indicator's state undefined.
checks.remediation: Set implementation_status on the indicator in the record store.

checks.title: Indicator meets the automated method minimum for its class
checks.requirement: Class A MAY implement automated methods; Class B SHOULD have at least 1 per indicator; Class C MUST have at least 2; Class D MUST have at least 4.
checks.risk: Falling short of the class minimum is a direct rule shortfall that blocks the certification class being sought.
checks.remediation: Add automated methods until the class minimum is met, or drop to a class whose minimum you meet.

checks.title: Record was built from the pinned rules dataset
checks.requirement: The record must reflect the version of the FedRAMP rules it claims to answer.
checks.risk: A record built from a superseded dataset can answer rules that have since changed or been withdrawn.
checks.remediation: Re-pull the dataset, diff it, then rerun the full pipeline.

checks.title: Record exists in both human-readable and JSON form
checks.requirement: Providers MUST supply a Security Decision Record in both human-readable and JSON formats.
checks.risk: Supplying only one format fails the rule outright, whichever format is missing.
checks.remediation: Run build_sdr.py, which emits both from the single record store.

checks.title: The two formats agree on every identifier and status
checks.requirement: Providers MUST use automation to ensure information remains consistent between human-readable and machine-readable formats.
checks.risk: Divergent formats mean one of them is wrong, and an assessor reading the human-readable copy would reach conclusions the JSON contradicts.
checks.remediation: Never hand-edit either rendering. Edit the record store and regenerate so both come from one source.

checks.title: Human-readable rendering contains no markup symbols
checks.requirement: The human-readable format has to actually be readable by a person without a renderer.
checks.risk: Raw markup in a deliverable reads as sloppy and can obscure meaning in print or plain-text delivery.
checks.remediation: Keep markup out of the human-readable renderer and the record store content.

checks.title: Machine-readable record validates against the official FedRAMP schema
checks.requirement: Providers MUST supply machine-readable information in JSON documents that are valid against the corresponding FedRAMP JSON schema.
checks.risk: An invalid document cannot be ingested by FedRAMP or by an agency's governance tooling, so the submission is not usable evidence.
checks.remediation: Fix the reported schema paths, then regenerate. Do not edit generated JSON by hand.

checks.title: Record carries version, last update and update source
checks.requirement: Providers MUST include version, date and time of last update, and source of update in their Security Decision Record.
checks.risk: Without these an assessor cannot tell which revision they are reading or who changed it, so no finding can be tied to a version.
checks.remediation: Set sdr_version and sdr_last_updated in the offering profile and regenerate.

checks.title: No account identifiers, keys or private key material in the record
checks.requirement: Certification Data is published, so it must not carry secrets or account identifiers.
checks.risk: Publishing an account identifier or key turns a compliance deliverable into a targeting aid, and a leaked key is an incident.
checks.remediation: Remove the value from the record store, rotate anything exposed, and regenerate.

checks.title: Record links to the Certification Package Overview
checks.requirement: Providers MUST supply a Certification Package Overview, and the Security Decision Record schema requires a URI pointing to it.
checks.risk: An assessor landing on the record has no route to the offering's scope, boundary or service description.
checks.remediation: Set certification_package_overview_uri in the offering profile to the published overview URI.

checks.title: Record has been updated recently enough to be current
checks.requirement: Providers SHOULD implement automated methods to persistently verify and validate the accuracy and completeness of the Security Decision Record.
checks.risk: A record that has not moved in months is not a persistent record; an assessor cannot treat it as describing the live system.
checks.remediation: Refresh the record from current facts and bump sdr_last_updated on every content change.
